title: Staff Platform Product Manager, Payments Regional Growth
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

At Airbnb, if there’s anything related to money, it comes to the Payments team. We are building a world-class payments and commerce organization - one that currently supports 191+ countries, 70 currencies, connects dozens of payment providers and banks, processes multiple billions of dollars, and empowers more people to participate in our global marketplace.

We’re looking for people who know and use Airbnb and believe in what we’re trying to accomplish. Airbnb is a marketplace that connects guests and hosts, and Payments is central to creating the trust that makes every transaction possible.

The Platform team plays the role of conductor, bringing together engineers, designers, and data scientists to build great product experiences. Our Payments Platform Managers own outcomes across foundation, growth, and empowerment, setting the vision and strategy, defining the roadmap, and driving execution.

The Difference You Will Make:

Latin America is one of the fastest-growing and most strategically important payments regions for Airbnb. Winning here means navigating complex, market-specific regulation, deep local payment ecosystems, and fast-moving compliance requirements across Brazil, Mexico, and the broader region — while unlocking meaningful growth through local payment methods, checkout optimization, and installments. We're hiring a Product Manager to own this regional payments portfolio end to end and serve as the product leader for one of Payments' highest-impact areas.

A Typical Day:

  • Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for regional payments across Brazil, Mexico, and the broader region — prioritizing across regulatory, growth, and platform work.
  • Optimize checkout and conversion — reduce friction at the moment of booking, improve regional checkout conversion funnels, and lift authorization/approval and payment-success rates to grow bookings.
  • Grow through local payment methods and affordability products — expand local payment methods and installment/affordability options that improve access and conversion for regional guests.
  • Drive the full product lifecycle — discovery, PRDs, launch, ramp (ERF), and iteration — using experiments and A/B tests to validate impact.
  • Define product requirements for processor and payment-method integrations, partnering with the Partnerships and Engineering teams on delivery and performance.
  • Lead regulatory and compliance workstreams in partnership with Legal, Tax, Compliance, and Finance to meet local market requirements.
  • Define and track KPIs across conversion, cost, reliability, and revenue, and use data to prioritize and measure impact.
  • Monitor the market — regulatory change, competitor moves, and emerging payment rails — and translate it into the roadmap.
  • Partner cross-functionally across Engineering, Design, Analytics, Data Science, Finance, Compliance/Legal, Partnerships, and Country teams to execute a shared vision without direct authority.

Your Expertise:

  • 10+ years of product management experience, with a strong track record building and scaling payments or financial products — owning strategy, roadmap, and execution.
  • Deep understanding of the payments stack and how money moves in a marketplace environment — across payins, payouts, and the flow of funds.
  • Strong checkout and conversion instincts — a demonstrated ability to reduce friction at the moment of purchase and improve funnel conversion.
  • Hands-on experience with payments fundamentals: authorization and settlement, processors/gateways and acquirers, card-scheme rules, 3DS/SCA, tokenization/vaulting, and reconciliation.
  • Experience with local payment methods and affordability products (e.g., wallets, bank transfers, BNPL/installments).
  • Familiarity with the LATAM payments ecosystem — Pix, SPEI (Mexico's real-time interbank transfers), regional wallets, and installment culture ("parcelamento" / "meses sin intereses") — and local regulatory frameworks (e.g., Central Bank of Brazil, SAT Mexico).
  • Data-driven: fluent in defining KPIs, running experiments, and using analytics to guide decisions.
  • Technical acumen to partner closely with engineering and explain complex concepts simply.
  • Strong product thinking and user empathy — able to imagine the ideal experience and work backwards from customer needs.
  • English required; Portuguese and/or Spanish strongly preferred.

Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging:

Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

How We'll Take Care of You:

title: Senior Technical Program Manager
description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Technical Program Manager, Performance and Infrastructure – Engineering PMO

Cloudflare is seeking a highly skilled, self-motivated Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead strategic, multi-quarter initiatives within our Performance and Infrastructure organization. As a vital link between Product, Engineering, Capacity Planning, Finance, and Reliability, you will drive a unified strategy from initial conception through to successful execution.

In this role, you will be deeply involved in gathering requirements, defining deliverables, and reporting on progress. You will manage stakeholder expectations, proactively identify risks and dependencies, and ensure the delivery of predictable, high-impact outcomes.

The ideal candidate is process-oriented yet remains flexible and iterative. You excel at navigating ambiguous technical challenges, fostering collaboration across teams, and asking the insightful questions necessary to drive stakeholders toward measurable results. This position requires a professional capable of managing complex tradeoffs and coordinating teams across global time zones.

Key Responsibilities

As a Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM), you will be responsible for a portfolio of foundational infrastructure initiatives, including program planning, execution cadence and leadership reporting and alignment. This role is a product-minded TPM position that combines technical program discipline with shaping program vision, customer needs, use cases, success measures, and roadmap tradeoffs. This role requires a strong blend of technical acumen, strategic thinking, and organizational leadership.

Program and Portfolio Leadership

  • Strategic Planning: Lead execution for key initiatives, focusing on Infrastructure Efficiency and Engineering Reliability.

  • Leadership Alignment: Partner with Product and Engineering leaders to establish goals, metrics, and decision frameworks.

  • Portfolio Visibility: Maintain program plans, roadmaps, dependency maps, and executive status reports.

  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Align Product, Engineering, Infrastructure, Capacity, Data, Finance, Ops, and Security teams.

  • Decision Management: Identify tradeoffs early, document decisions, and manage escalations to resolution.

  • Customer Representation: Represent internal technical users and integrate their workflows into program planning.

Infrastructure Efficiency

An overview of this role

Credit-based and consumption-based offerings are becoming central to how GitLab monetizes. The systems that meter, rate, and bill that consumption sit underneath all of it. You'll own the backend usage billing pipeline and its product direction while supporting the Monetization Platform and Infrastructure team as it modernizes the foundations underneath it.

When another GitLab team launches a credit-consuming capability, you'll help them make it billable across GitLab.com, self-managed, and GitLab Dedicated. This is a technical, systems-oriented product role: success means building a monetization platform other teams can launch on quickly and correctly, rather than shipping customer-facing UI.

What you’ll do

  • Own the product direction for metering, aggregation, and rating in GitLab's usage billing pipeline, including the Zuora and CustomersDot integrations that turn usage into invoiced revenue.

  • Prioritize pipeline scalability, performance, and reliability as consumption grows, balancing those investments against new capability enablement.
  • Own billing defect detection and remediation so errors surface before they reach a customer's invoice and billing outcomes remain auditable.
  • Support the Monetization Platform and Infrastructure team by framing problems, explaining the value of platform investments, and prioritizing them against operational risk.
  • Define and track measures of billing accuracy, pipeline reliability, cost to serve per capability, and time to monetize so teams can make informed pricing decisions.

  • Experience owning the product direction of consumption- or usage-based billing systems.
  • Experience with Zuora or a comparable billing and revenue platform, and an understanding of how product and finance systems interact.
  • Experience with prepaid, commitment, or credit-drawdown pricing models (balances, reservations, overage, expiration) and the edge cases they create in billing and revenue.
  • Experience launching new products or pricing models while coordinating across engineering, Finance, Legal, Compliance and go-to-market teams.

In Monetization, we coordinate across engineering, Finance, Legal, Compliance and go-to-market on new products and pricing models. Our remote, asynchronous work uses written issues, and epics to keep decisions visible.

Remote-Global

You'll have direct influence over how we shape the team's future operating model.

Internal Product Roadmap Ownership

  • Define, own, and maintain the multi-quarter internal product roadmap for the Lead-to-Opportunity domain covering lead capture, enrichment, scoring, routing, conversion, opportunity and the broader GTM technology stack integrated with Salesforce
  • Translate business strategy from Marketing, Sales Development, RevOps, and GTM leadership into sequenced, prioritized system capabilities with clear outcomes and success metrics
  • Define the domain's strategic priorities each quarter and half, balancing net-new capability delivery, stabilization, and technical debt reduction with transparent trade-off frameworks
  • Drive quarterly planning ceremonies, partnering with Engineering Managers and BSAs to align capacity with roadmap commitments
  • Own domain-level documentation: process maps, current-vs-future state lead lifecycle flows, and decision logs that keep stakeholders and the team aligned on scope and ownership

Stakeholder Partnership & Requirements Translation

  • Serve as the primary product voice for all L2O and GTM Systems initiatives, partnering closely with Marketing, Marketing Operations, SDR/BDR leadership, Sales, and RevOps
  • Lead discovery, requirements workshops, and business process design sessions translating complex GTM and marketing operations requirements into actionable system specifications
  • Own the decision layer between "what the business needs" and "what engineering builds," resolving ambiguity with structured frameworks and documented decisions
  • Run structured stakeholder alignment sessions to surface trade-offs, build consensus, and drive open decisions to closure rather than letting them linger
  • Represent the domain in cross-team planning and leadership reviews able to explain technical constraints to business stakeholders and business context to engineers

  • Act as a product craft mentor and senior thought partner for the BSA team, actively upskilling analysts in product thinking, requirements structuring, acceptance criteria definition, and roadmap communication
  • Model and codify what "good" looks like reusable templates, rituals (backlog grooming, roadmap reviews), and a rubric BSAs can grow against
  • Give BSAs increasing ownership over pieces of the roadmap as they develop, with regular feedback and structured check-ins
  • Partner with leadership to evolve the team's operating model from project-execution-focused to product-thinking-led, raising the bar for how EntApps delivers business value

Program Strategy & Delivery Oversight

  • Lead initiatives end-to-end: discovery, requirements, prioritization, solution design review, UAT, launch, and post-launch measurement
  • Write and maintain clear user stories, acceptance criteria, and lead-flow and data-flow diagrams that engineering and admins can build against without ambiguity
  • Manage a healthy, well-groomed backlog intake requests from Marketing and Sales Development, triage by impact and effort, and defend prioritization decisions to stakeholders
  • Define success metrics per initiative (lead response time, routing accuracy, lead-to-opportunity conversion rate, data quality, SDR/BDR adoption) and report on outcomes, not just delivery
  • Identify and de-risk dependencies across adjacent domains campaign operations, data enrichment vendors, opportunity handoff to sales before they block delivery
  • Own UAT strategy and acceptance criteria in collaboration with BSAs, ensuring system changes meet business requirements before production release

Systems Architecture Collaboration

  • Partner with Enterprise Architects and Engineering Managers on Salesforce and MarTech integration design marketing automation platform to Salesforce sync, data enrichment pipelines, lead scoring and routing engines, ensuring choices hold up to governance, scale, and future roadmap needs
  • Bring informed opinions on GTM platform architecture trade-offs based on deep domain knowledge
  • Stay current on platform roadmaps for Salesforce Sales Cloud and connected MarTech tools, identifying opportunities to leverage native capabilities before custom builds
  • Maintain domain-level R&R clarity, who owns what across US/India technical managers, BSAs, and adjacent pods and update as team and scope evolve
  • Ability to engage deeply with engineering and architecture teams on API design, data modeling, and integration patterns.

What You'll Bring

  • 7+ years in Salesforce product management, business systems analysis, or Marketing/Revenue Operations technology roles, with demonstrated growth into product ownership
  • Strong working knowledge of Lead-to-Opportunity processes; lead capture, scoring, routing, and conversion and how they connect marketing execution to sales pipeline
  • Hands-on familiarity with the GTM technology stack: Salesforce Sales Cloud plus marketing automation platforms (Marketo, HubSpot, or Pardot), lead scoring and routing tools, and data enrichment or intent providers
  • Good Understanding of quoting process
  • Demonstrated ability to own and communicate multi-quarter internal product roadmaps to senior business and technology stakeholders
  • Proven experience leading initiatives end-to-end with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities, especially across Marketing and Sales
  • Sufficient technical fluency to engage meaningfully with engineering on API design, data model decisions, and integration trade-offs — without needing to write code
  • Experience mentoring or upskilling analysts and BSAs, you enjoy developing people, not just managing tickets
  • Excellent written and verbal communication; able to represent technical trade-offs to non-technical executives and translate business asks into clear technical requirements
  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity and driving structure where none exists
  • Experience with AI-assisted development workflows, data governance and compliance for lead data, or prior people-management experience

You'll be one of the first product managers on a team actively transforming from a reactive BSA function into a proactive, roadmap-driven product organization. description:

Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. Private markets have been closed to everyday investors for decades.   • Experience working with 3rd-party partners on large-scale projects to deliver a shared product

title: Program Manager, Safeguards Policy, Enforcement, and Threat Intelligence
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Safeguards organization builds the policies, evaluations, and detection and enforcement systems that define and hold the limits on how Claude can be used. Within Safeguards, our Policy, Enforcement, and Threat Intelligence teams work as one org: Policy Design defines what is and isn't allowed across harm areas, Enforcement detects and acts on violations, and Threat Intelligence investigates sophisticated misuse and emerging threats.

That work runs across a lot of teams and moves fast. A single decision can touch model training, detection systems, product launches, legal review, and external communications. As the org's program manager, you'll keep all of it moving: tracking the portfolio across all three teams, running the processes that connect their work to each other and to the rest of the company, and making sure the right people are aligned before decisions land.

Your work will include the operating rhythm (planning, priorities, status, and decision tracking), launch and release readiness across policy, enforcement, and threat intelligence workstreams, and the processes that support how we share our work externally, including blog posts, threat reports, and other publications. You'll work closely with the org's leadership to spot risks early, clear blockers, and keep everyone pointed in the same direction.

This role is a good fit for someone who brings structure to ambiguous, fast-moving work without adding overhead, and who can earn the trust of policy experts, researchers, and engineers alike.

Important context for this role: some of the work may involve exposure to explicit content, including material of a sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing nature. It also may require late nights or weekend work.

Key responsibilities

  • Own cross-functional program management for the Policy Design, Enforcement and Threat Intel teams, keeping workstreams across harm areas on track and visible to leadership

  • Run the team's operating rhythm: quarterly planning, priority setting, status tracking, and a clear record of decisions, who made them, and why

  • Coordinate policy work with partner teams across research, product, engineering, legal, and communications, so dependencies are surfaced early and nothing lands on a partner as a surprise

  • Drive readiness for policy, enforcement, and threat intelligence work tied to model launches and product releases, including timelines, reviews, and sign-offs

  • Own the process for the org's external publications, including blog posts and threat reports, from idea through drafting, review, approvals, and publication

  • Identify risks, blockers, and resourcing gaps across the portfolio, and escalate them with a proposed path forward

  • Build lightweight processes and tools that make the team faster, and retire the ones that stop earning their keep

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience running cross-functional programs in a fast-moving technical environment, with a track record of shipping on time across teams you don't manage

  • Ability to bring structure to ambiguous work: breaking big goals into plans, owners, and milestones, and keeping them current as priorities shift

  • Strong written communication, including clear status updates, decision records, and summaries for executive audiences

  • Experience managing review and approval processes with multiple stakeholders, such as publications, launches, or policy releases

  • Judgment about when a process helps and when it's overhead, and a bias toward the lightest process that works

  • Comfort working on sensitive topics and holding high standards for confidentiality

Preferred qualifications

  • Program management experience in trust & safety, product policy, enforcement operations, threat intelligence, or AI safety

  • Familiarity with how AI models are developed and launched, and how policy, enforcement, and threat intelligence work plug into that cycle

  • Experience coordinating external publications, research releases, or public communications

  • Experience using AI tools, including agentic tools, to automate tracking, reporting, and other recurring program work

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$285,000—$330,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Senior Product Manager - Application Protection & Governance
description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations: London, Lisbon, or New York

About the Role

As a Senior Product Manager for Application Protection & Governance, you’ll join our core Application Security team to protect web, API applications against evolving abuse and threat patterns. You will own the product outcomes that help customers deploy, operate, and improve security controls over time, turning complex security requirements into practical capabilities and operational guidance.

In this role, you will partner with engineering, security specialists and the go-to-market organization to define product direction and drive adoption across areas including web, LLM and API protection (for example, profiling and validation of traffic patterns, schema-aware enforcement, and reducing risks from interconnected third- and fourth-party integrations). You’ll also establish measurement and feedback loops to assess effectiveness, reduce customer operational friction, and continuously iterate based on real-world results.

You’ll be the strategic anchor for these initiatives aligning customer needs, internal safety requirements, and technical feasibility to deliver reliable protection for applications at global scale.

Responsibilities

  • End-to-End Product Ownership: Own the entire user journey for your product portfolio, ensuring a seamless experience across both programmatic APIs and user-facing dashboards (UX). Collaborate closely with design teams to build intuitive, developer-friendly interfaces.
  • Roadmap & Strategy: Deeply understand the application security landscape and analyze customer pain points to define, prioritize, and own the product roadmap.
  • Voice of the Customer: Meet regularly with customers and partners to gather direct feedback, understand real-world deployment challenges, and continuously inject customer insights back into the product lifecycle.
  • Iterative Execution: Partner with engineering and the broader application security organization to ship impactful features. At Cloudflare, we are biased for action, we prioritize shipping early, gathering data, and iterating rapidly.
  • Go-to-Market & Documentation: Own all customer-facing communications and technical documentation, ensuring complex security features are easily understood and adopted by our users.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Serve as the primary point of contact for your products, both internally and externally.
  • Sales & Support Enablement: Actively support the sales organization across all stages of customer engagement (pre-sales strategy and post-sales expansion and adoption). Collaborate tightly with Customer Support to resolve technical issues and incidents.

Key Qualifications

  • Proven Product Management Experience: 4+ years of experience as a Product Manager successfully delivering high-scale cloud solutions targeted at a technical audience within the B2B SaaS industry.
  • Customer Focus: Ability to design for massive enterprises without compromising the experience for individual developers and small businesses. You excel at balancing the diverse needs of Cloudflare's broad user base.
  • Deep Technical Acumen: Comfortable engaging in deep technical discussions with engineering teams. You can quickly grasp complex security concepts and translate them into clear, compelling narratives for customers through blog posts, whitepapers, and direct calls.
  • AI-Driven Productivity: Embrace and actively adopt advanced AI tools to work autonomously, streamline product management workflows, and maximize efficiency to ship high-quality products faster.
  • Preferred Experience: Professional background in web security, API security, application security, or cloud security infrastructure is highly preferred.

Compensation

Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location.

  • For New York City based hires: Estimated annual salary of $156,000 - $210,000

Benefits

Cloudflare offers a complete package of benefits and programs to support you and your family. Our benefits programs can help you pay health care expenses, support caregiving, build capital for the future and make life a little easier and fun! The below is a description of our benefits for employees in the United States, and benefits may vary for employees based outside the U.S.

Health & Welfare Benefits

  • Medical/Rx Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Commuter Spending Accounts
  • Fertility & Family Forming Benefits
  • On-demand mental health support and Employee Assistance Program

About the Role

More than 50% of Internet traffic is automated. Knowing who's human, who's an agent, and who's a malicious actor is core to Cloudflare's strategy, and one of the primary values we sell to our Customers. We're building the products that answer "can we trust this traffic?" and our story is differentiated, but the demand is outpacing the number of experts who can tell our story. This role will drive the solution to this challenge.

We think of this as the next generation of product marketing, built for a technical product and rebuilt as a part of the Product team. At Cloudflare, PMs are the first sellers, and own their own launches, content, and enablement. This role, like the rest of the team, will be both deep in R&D as well as in the field driving real Customer conversations, feeling firsthand what lands, and turning that into the enablement, materials, and programs the entire field runs on. Your credibility comes from carrying the pitch yourself.

You will work directly with the Director of Product and across the PMs who lead each product line. As a member of the product team, your work in the field shapes the strategy and the narrative. You own how far and how fast that story travels, and how well the field can carry it on its own.

What you'll do

Own the field's ability to win.

Build the enablement that lets any account team lead a conversation about agents, bots, attackers, or fraud, end to end. This includes training, playbooks, battlecards, demo environments, proof-of-concept guides, competitive intelligence, and certification. You are measured by how capable you make the entire field, and by how much you free up product experts to build rather than sell.

Carry the pitch as a member of the Product team.

Join and drive real Customer calls. This keeps your enablement grounded in what actually works. You will stand up and orchestrate a bench of field subject-matter experts who scale this well beyond one person.

Amplify our story.

Our space is presented through some of the most engaging material in the company, closer to an interactive application than a slide deck. You will extend and evolve that into assets the field can run on its own, and produce new material of the same caliber.

Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations: Austin or London (Hybrid)

About the Role

We're hiring the first embedded Lead Product Designer for Cloudflare's Web Integrity & Trust product suite. More than 50% of Internet traffic is automated. Knowing who's human, who's an agent, and who's a malicious actor is core to Cloudflare's strategy, and one of the primary values we sell to our customers.

Cloudflare sits in front of more than 20% of the web. That vantage point lets us detect automated threats, fraud, and traffic manipulation at a scale and depth no one else can match. Turning that raw signal into something a human can understand, trust, and act on is one of the most interesting design problems in security today — and it's the problem you'll own.

Our products make probabilistic decisions in an adversarial environment. “Is this traffic truthfully representing who they are?” and "Can we trust this traffic?" doesn't have a clean yes-or-no answer. Our objective is to minimize risk without ever having ground truth. Your job is to make that kind of reasoning legible and controllable to the people who rely on it, from the security analyst running an investigation to the marketing team trying to understand the performance of their most recent campaign.

This role spans the full arc of how customers work with our product suite, from navigation, configuration, exploring and investigating their traffic, to proving the value of what Cloudflare's network sees. Today those experiences live in disconnected places; a core part of this role is envisioning the coherent product they should become. This role will work directly with the Director of Product and across the PMs who lead each product line

title: Technical Program Manager, Life Sciences
region: San Francisco, CA / New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

Scientists use Claude across the life sciences, from drug discovery and research biology to clinical development and manufacturing. To support that work, Anthropic introduced the Life Sciences Verification Program (LSVP), which gives verified life science professionals access to Claude with a refined set of safeguards that is more permissive for biology-related work. The program is in beta.We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to own the program of work that expands that access and helps scale it with safety in mind.

Each expansion depends on many teams at once and no single team owns the path end to end. You'll become the single owner of that program, the person who knows what each expansion requires, where every workstream stands, what it is waiting on, and who needs to decide. This is a cross-org execution role, not a research role, and it does not require a life sciences background. LSVP is the starting point, and the scope will grow alongside Anthropic's broader work in the life sciences. Over time, more of the life sciences community can get verified access, and each new expansion takes less bespoke effort than the last.

Responsibilities

  • Own the program for expanding access to Anthropic's life sciences verification programs: scoping, sequencing, dependencies, and tradeoffs across safeguards, platform, and product engineering teams
  • Scope and drive the cross-org engineering work that each expansion requires, from new plan and account types to new platforms
  • Partner with the product manager to turn program goals into a sequenced plan with clear owners and dates
  • Drive clarity on data access, retention, and review requirements, and on the changes they require across safeguards, access, and provisioning
  • Drive user experience scoping across the Claude product surfaces where the program is available
  • Find and remove the technical blockers that keep eligible organizations from accessing life sciences capabilities
  • Establish the operating rhythm: a single view of workstreams, owners, dependencies, risks, and status, with planning, escalation paths, and launch coordination across orgs
  • Convert recurring efforts into documented, repeatable processes so that each new expansion requires less bespoke coordination

You may be a good fit if you

  • Have several years of experience in technical program management, with a track record of successfully delivering complex, cross-functional programs
  • Have experience coordinating across multiple engineering teams and organizations simultaneously, including safeguards, platform, and product partners
  • Can engage meaningfully with the engineers doing the work, from platform and access systems to product surfaces
  • Are highly organized and can manage multiple parallel workstreams effectively across distributed teams
  • Thrive in unstructured environments with a knack for bringing order to chaos and creating clarity in ambiguous situations
  • Have excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence without authority
  • Have worked on cloud or platform programs (preferred but not required)
  • Do not need a life sciences background. This is not a research role, and no life sciences experience is required
  • Are passionate about Anthropic's mission and interested in the challenges of bringing AI capabilities to the life sciences community safely and reliably

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$290,000—$365,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

An overview of this role

As Principal Program Manager, Go-To-Market, you own two equal pillars of go-to-market execution for Product & Technical Marketing (PTM). First, you are the strategic and hands-on architect behind GitLab's high-stakes minor and major launches, redesigning the launch operating model with AI agents at its core so customers discover, adopt, and experience GitLab with precision.

Second, you run program management on key initiatives that span Product Management and Product Design through Growth Marketing, Comms and Social, and Field Enablement, wherever those motions depend on PTM. PTM team is responsible for product and solutions marketing, technical writing and documentation, developer advocacy, and globalization, and acts as the glue between these functions across a variety of go-to-market initiatives.

You are AI-first by default. When programs still run on many manual steps, you convert that work into team-wide AI workflows, either by shipping the automations yourself or by partnering with the AI Transformation Owner (ATO) for the marketing organization to drive shared skills, adoption, and governance. You are not a reactive deadline chaser. You drive solutions with stakeholders as dates approach, design decision stages so tradeoffs land early, and redesign stages and workflows when product roadmap, growth priorities, or major launch decisions change. You create clarity in ambiguity: frame the problem, present options and tradeoffs, name owners, and optimize for decision velocity.

In your first year, you institutionalize a dual operating system: a scalable launch framework for 15+ minor and major launches per year, and a portfolio program practice that maps dependencies from Product and Design through PTM into Growth, Comms, and Field. You ship production agent workflows that cut manual coordination, establish benchmarks for quality, and make go-to-market program management achieve relevance in the AI era, and become a trusted partner across the organization.

Reporting to the VP of Product & Technical Marketing, you operate with significant executive visibility and autonomy. You measure success by what lands for customers and the business: pipeline where it matters, and brand and community impact where business requires it, not by activity volume alone.

Some examples of projects:

  • Orchestrate minor launches that put new platform releases in front of the community
  • Orchestrate major launches tied to company events that move pipeline
  • Orchestrate weekly signal announcements so we stay present in a fast-moving ecosystem
  • Sequence product decisions into PTM and other go-to-market functions, with clear handoffs
  • Keep field enablement on track when they depend on messaging and sales assets
  • Design decision points early so blockers show up before the deadline
  • Scope launches for pipeline and for post-launch adoption when agentic products are involved
  • Build AI workflows that draft briefs, synthesize status, and cut manual program steps
  • Rebuild stages and calendars when roadmap, growth priorities, or launch plans change
  • Run retrospectives that improve the system, and remove process as often as you add it

What you'll do

  • Run a concurrent portfolio of PTM-dependent initiatives with clear owners, dates, and tradeoffs
  • Give leadership the context to decide: risks, options, and a recommendation, not status theater
  • Align go-to-market functions when work streams collide or compete for the same people
  • Codify how programs run so each cycle starts sharper than the last
  • Put quality in the path of the work, then confirm market-facing pieces landed as intended
  • Turn recurring coordination into shared AI workflows the team can run without you in the loop
  • Partner with Marketing's ATO when a workflow needs department-wide adoption or guardrails
  • Escalate early with a clear ask when a call sits above the working team
  • Protect focus with smaller core teams, fewer standing meetings, more working sessions
  • Close the loop on results with the data team, then feed what you learn into the next cycle

What you'll bring

  • Program management for go-to-market across the high-tech industry, with first-hand experience with complex, multi-stakeholder and cross-functional initiatives.
  • Experience building and scaling how programs run in large, distributed orgs, with clear results
  • Hands-on work with AI agents and automations that real teams used in production
  • A track record of turning manual work into AI workflows and helping others adopt them
  • Comfort standing up launch and program frameworks without adding busywork
  • Strong grasp of how product releases and how they impact go-to-market teams
  • Bias to action for priorities: defining risks and clear options for path forward
  • Habit of measuring success by pipeline, adoption, or consumption, not activity counts
  • Ability to run several high-stakes workstreams at once without dropping quality or trust

  • Influence without direct authority, including with senior leaders
  • Fluency with project tools with AI automation on top, and the ability to use GitLab
  • Ability to travel if needed and comply with the company's travel policy

About the team

Product & Technical Marketing at GitLab is the engine behind how GitLab positions, launches, documents, and evangelizes its value proposition for enterprises worldwide. We connect GitLab's product capabilities to customers and prospects across technical personas and executive buyers, and we partner closely with Product Management, Product Design, Growth Marketing, Comms and Social, Field Enablement, Sales, and the broader go-to-market organization so what we build lands in market with clarity, impact, and relevance. We operate as one marketing organization with clear roles: PTM carries the message; Growth activates demand; Comms amplifies narrative; work moves when handoffs are explicit.

You serve as the senior operational and program spine inside Product & Technical Marketing. You translate roadmap and positioning strategy into coordinated launches and PTM-dependent initiatives across the go-to-market chain, while building the playbooks and AI-powered workflows that make excellence repeatable at scale. We are building towards an operational model where agents handle the scaffolding of cross-functional programs, freeing team members to focus on strategy and judgement.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. An overview of this role

As a Senior Product Manager, you will own GitLab's Secret Detection offering and the Vulnerability Research function that produces the detection content across security products. Secret Detection is one of the highest-signal, highest-volume security capabilities on the platform. Leaked credentials are the most common initial access vector in real breaches, and as AI agents write, commit, and configure more of the software, the surface area for exposed secrets grows faster than the number of humans watching it.

You will own the full loop: detect a secret with high precision, tell the customer whether it is still live, get it revoked, and prevent the next one from ever landing. In parallel, you will own vulnerability research as a product asset rather than a back-office function. The detection rules, advisory data, and malicious package and reference intelligence your team produces are what make GitLab's security scanners worth paying for, and they need to ship on a cadence with measurable quality.

This is an outcome-owning role - you will carry adoption, retention, and revenue targets for your area and be expected to explain how your roadmap moves them.

Some examples of our projects:

  • Push protection and pre-receive blocking that stops a credential before it reaches a repository, without wrecking developer flow
  • Secret validity checking and automated revocation partnerships with major cloud and SaaS token issuers
  • Detection content pipelines that turn threat research into shipped rules, with precision and recall tracked per rule
  • Intelligence-driven detection of malicious packages, dependencies, and references entering the software supply chain

What you'll do

  • Own the business outcomes for Secret Detection and Vulnerability Research, including adoption, expansion, competitive win rate, and revenue contribution. Bring a point of view on packaging and pricing, not just features.
  • Set the strategy for the full secret lifecycle: prevention, detection, validation, revocation, and reporting across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed.
  • Treat detection content as a product. Define how rules, advisories, and intelligence feeds are sourced, validated, versioned, and measured, and make quality visible to customers.
  • Hold the line on detection quality. False positives are a product defect and you will own the metrics that prove precision is improving.
  • Work at the level of the technology. Read the rule syntax, question the entropy heuristics, understand why a scanner missed something, and challenge engineering with informed alternatives.
  • Use AI to compress the distance between question and answer. Pull your own data, prototype your own flows, synthesize research and competitive input yourself, and bring conclusions rather than requests for someone else to investigate.
  • Build the case for where AI belongs in the product: triage, rule generation, remediation guidance, and reducing the human review burden per finding.
  • Partner with engineering, security research, threat intelligence, Field, and GitLab's own Security team, who are one of your most demanding users.
  • Communicate in writing, asynchronously, with enough precision that a distributed team can act without a meeting.

What you'll bring

  • Domain depth in application security, vulnerability management, or security research. You have worked on or adjacent to scanners, detection content, threat intelligence, or SDLC security tooling and you know how these products actually get evaluated in a bake-off.
  • Technical credibility sufficient to earn the respect of a security engineering team. You do not need to have written the scanner, but you should be able to reason about detection logic, data pipelines, CI integration, and the tradeoffs between coverage and noise.
  • Commercial reasoning. You start from revenue mechanics, buyer motion, and competitive displacement, then work inward to product decisions. Candidates who reason only from feature lists outward are not a fit.
  • Evidence of using AI as a force multiplier in your own work: research, analysis, data pulls, prototyping, drafting. Consuming a chat assistant occasionally is not the same as restructuring how you work.
  • Judgment under ambiguity. You bring structured options and a recommendation instead of escalating an open question.
  • Bias for clarity. You can take a noisy, technical, politically contested problem and produce one page that everyone can align on.
  • Bonus: hands-on background as a developer, security engineer, red teamer, or researcher; experience with credential and token ecosystems; experience commercializing a data or intelligence asset.

About the team

This role sits in GitLab's Security product management organization, which owns application security testing, vulnerability management, supply chain security, secrets management, and AI governance. The Security Section is central to GitLab's Ultimate tier and to the shift toward consumption-based product revenue, so the work is visible to senior leadership and directly tied to company results. You will work asynchronously with engineering, design, and research counterparts across multiple regions, and with the Field teams who take this to market.

In this position you will be the owner of the roadmap for discounts and promotions and how they work within our broader set of pricing tools for the millions of hosts in our community. title: Associate Product Manager (New Grad)
description:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

From day one, we've been breaking down barriers, empowering people with the tools, knowledge, and products to participate in the financial system. Our innovation doesn't stop — and we need bright, curious minds to help shape the future of finance!

As an Associate Product Manager, you'll be at the center of our product innovation. You'll work alongside top talent from engineering, design, research, and more to bring groundbreaking financial products to life. From simplifying complex financial processes to crafting seamless customer experiences, your work will help shape the future of fintech. This role offers direct mentorship from some of the most accomplished product leaders in the industry, giving you the chance to grow, learn, and make a real impact in a fast-paced, cutting-edge environment.

This role is based in our New York, NY office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Collaborate with engineering, design, research, data science, and marketing teams to deeply understand our customers and their most pressing needs
  • Define and execute product strategies that align with business goals and user expectations
  • Be the voice of the product, facilitating communication and collaboration across teams
  • Lead product launches, ensuring they are delivered on time and meet a high standard of quality
  • Set and monitor KPIs to measure success and track product engagement and adoption

What you bring

title: Senior Compliance Program Manager, Political Law
region: San Francisco, CA / New York City, NY / Washington, DC
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Integrity & Compliance function is building the systems that let us scale responsibly as our products reach more people, more enterprises, and more governments. Corporate Compliance is a key pillar of that function, covering anti-bribery and anti-corruption, conflicts of interest, gifts and hospitality, outside activities, the Code of Conduct, and related employee-conduct matters.

As Senior Compliance Program Manager, you will build and run Anthropic's political law compliance program — the operating infrastructure behind our corporate PAC, corporate political giving, state and local pay-to-play preclearance, and the gift and ethics rules governing our interactions with public officials. As the program develops, the role may also extend to oversight of lobbying registration and reporting. You'll own the program end to end: designing the workflows, registers and controls, doing the work directly where it belongs in-house, and directing and quality-checking outside political law counsel and compliance vendors where we use them. You'll be the day-to-day compliance partner to our Policy and Government Affairs teams, working in close partnership with Policy Legal, who own the substantive legal advice, and with the rest of Corporate Compliance on the anti-corruption side of government engagement.

Because we run lean, you may support certain workstreams in our broader corporate compliance program — gifts and hospitality, conflicts of interest, outside business activities and related day-to-day matters — and help design the AI-assisted workflows that let a small team cover a large surface area.

This is a builder's role. We're looking for someone who has run political law compliance programs hands-on, is equally comfortable doing the work and managing outside firms who do it, always knows where every preclearance request and filing stands, and can turn fifty-state complexity into simple processes the business will actually use.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the political contributions preclearance program: intake, covered-persons register, jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction pay-to-play screening against live and prospective public-sector business, recordkeeping, and periodic reconciliation

  • Support corporate PAC compliance operations in partnership with Policy, Finance and outside counsel — restricted-class eligibility controls, solicitation review workflow, FEC reporting oversight, and reconciliations

  • Maintain the corporate political giving log and vetting workflow for candidate, committee, 527 and c4 contributions, and integrate pay-to-play triggers into contract intake for public-sector deals

  • Depending on how the program is scoped, support or take on lobbying compliance oversight: keeping a consolidated view of registrations, deadlines and filing status, and working with the outside firms that prepare filings

  • Manage outside political law counsel and compliance vendors supporting these workstreams — scoping, inputs, quality, timeliness and budget — and recommend over time what should sit in-house versus outside

  • Run gifts and hospitality review for events and interactions involving public officials, applying federal, state and local gift and ethics rules alongside our anti-corruption standards; disposition routine matters and escalate edge cases

  • Review and disposition conflicts of interest, outside business activity and gifts and hospitality matters across the broader corporate compliance queue; help maintain the post-government-employment and recusal tracker

  • Build and deliver training, quick-reference guidance and intake how-tos for Policy, GTM and leadership; keep policies and procedures current as the footprint changes

  • Serve as product owner for AI-assisted intake, screening and case-management workflows in your areas — define requirements, run testing, decide what is automated versus human-reviewed, and report program metrics to leadership

  • Spot legal questions early and route them to Policy Legal or outside counsel with the facts assembled; keep I&C, Legal and outside counsel calibrated on risk

Minimum qualifications

  • Hands-on ownership of political law compliance programs — corporate PAC, campaign finance, pay-to-play preclearance and covered-persons tracking, lobbying registration and reporting, government gift and ethics rules — or a closely comparable multi-jurisdiction regulatory program

  • Track record building a program, not just operating one — designing preclearance or disclosure workflows, registers, filing calendars and controls from scratch or through a major redesign

  • Fluent enough to do the work directly and experienced enough to manage outside counsel and compliance vendors doing it — scoping, feeding inputs, checking quality, holding deadlines

  • Working fluency in the federal framework (FECA/FEC, LDA/HLOGA, House and Senate gift rules) and the shape of state and local variation; knows when a question is a legal call and hands it off cleanly

  • Strong project management and cross-functional execution with Policy/Government Affairs, Legal, Finance and executive stakeholders; clear, brief, business-usable writing

  • Sound judgment and discretion handling politically and personally sensitive information

Preferred qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in compliance program management

  • Experience in a corporate government affairs compliance function, a political law practice or compliance vendor, or a financial-services pay-to-play program (SEC Rule 206(4)-5, MSRB G-37, CFTC)

  • Range across the broader corporate compliance portfolio — gifts and hospitality, conflicts of interest, outside activities, anti-corruption — and appetite to learn what you haven't done yet

  • Exposure to non-US lobbying transparency regimes (EU Transparency Register, German Lobby register, Irish Regulation of Lobbying Act, UK)

  • Hands-on with compliance tooling (case management, GRC, disclosure platforms, workflow automation) and real interest in using AI to run compliance work better

  • Experience at a high-growth or technology company, or otherwise operating lean without large-team infrastructure

  • Relevant certification (e.g., CCEP) or paralegal/JD background is a plus, not a requirement; this is a program role, not a counsel role

Claude Science is an AI workbench that gives researchers a single environment for work that today spans dozens of disconnected tools — literature, specialized databases, scientific computing, analysis, and publication-ready outputs. Claude Science already renders protein structures, genome tracks, and chemical structures natively, and coordinates multi-agent workflows with built-in review for citation and calculation errors — and we're just getting started. We're growing the Claude Science product team. As a Product Manager on Claude Science, you will own a major area of the roadmap end to end — think expanding into new scientific fields, landing new model capabilities with researchers, or making the workbench ready for enterprise R&D teams — and help shape the overall product direction alongside the rest of the team. You'll partner directly with our research teams to make the models better at science, help decide which fields and workflows we go after next, and shape what it takes for Claude Science to be trusted in enterprise and regulated research environments.

We're looking for experienced product managers and founders with real scientific or technical depth: people who can hold their own in a conversation with a structural biologist or a computational chemist, get in the weeds of model transcripts and evals, and still zoom out to help define a product category. You thrive in ambiguity, uncover non-obvious use cases for nascent capabilities, and bring those insights back to research.

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Claude is now good at security work. It finds and fixes vulnerabilities in real codebases, triages alerts, and reasons about how an attacker would move through a system, and it improves with every model we ship. Many security platforms build on Claude and we shipped our first security product this year (Claude Security).

You'll lead the cybersecurity product at Anthropic. That means setting the strategy, deciding what we build and where we partner, shipping products, and being the company's voice with CISOs, security vendors, and researchers. Some of this is 0→1 (our first-party products are a few months old and the next ones don't exist yet) and some of it is scaling what already works. Security touches nearly every team at the company.

Key responsibilities

  • Set Anthropic's cybersecurity product portfolio strategy and be accountable for the results.
  • Ship security products. Vulnerability discovery and remediation in Claude Code today and a broader set of capabilities in the future.
  • Represent Anthropic on security externally, with CISOs, vendors, researchers, governments, and press.
  • Partner with research. Know where the model falls short on security tasks and help build a plan to improve.
  • Work with safeguards and policy on model access for Cybersecurity.
  • Keep the cross-functional threads moving across research, engineering, sales, safeguards, policy, legal, and comms.

Minimum qualifications

  • You've spent meaningful time in security, whether building security products, running a security team, or doing the work yourself in application security, detection and response, vulnerability research, or offensive security.
  • You've built products or businesses from scratch and taken them to paying customers.
  • You design for where the models will be rather than where they are. You treat what the model can't do yet as a research target with a reliability bar, and you know what to ship in the meantime.
  • You have strong product judgment and enough technical depth to read a finding and tell whether it's real.
  • You're willing to do the unglamorous work.
  • You communicate well with CISOs, researchers, and executives alike.

Preferred qualifications

  • 12+ years of experience building and shipping products, especially in the security space .
  • Fluency with AI products: evaluations, model behavior as part of the product surface
  • Technical background or experience working closely with infrastructure/platform teams
  • Strong technical judgment with ability to go deep on security and infrastructure topics
  • Structured thinking and ability to break down complex compliance requirements into shippable features

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$385,000—$460,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Anthropic's New Markets and Monetization team exists to bring transformational AI to every business. Model capabilities are compounding, and the Claude Platform is how businesses build with our models. Our job within the Claude Platform is to make sure that every industry, not just software, can build on frontier AI with our APIs and that everyone who builds on Claude prospers by it.

The work falls into two pillars that reinforce each other.

  1. Verticals: identifying and building for the next API markets.
  2. Monetization: the commercial machinery that lets the platform do business anywhere, with anyone: a single way for usage that flows through partners, resellers, and other platforms.

We're hiring the founding product managers onto this team, and this posting covers all of them. You will own one of the areas below outright, work day to day with a dedicated engineering lead and designer, and be measured on numbers that are company-level goals for the half. Almost none of this exists yet, so most weeks you will be the person defining the problem rather than receiving it.

  • Partner and platform billing. How usage that reaches Claude through a partner, reseller, or another platform is metered, attributed, and billed, and the program terms that go with it, so indirect volume can grow without our risk growing with it.

  • One account, and the startup path built on it. One login and one wallet across the API and Claude's subscriptions, so a builder's first commit, first production call, and first invoice are on a single plan.
  • A vertical. The platform strategy for a particular industry: what builders there need that the platform doesn't yet do, which bets to make, and shipping them with the vertical's own product and go-to-market partners.

  • Talk to every side of the ecosystem, from enterprise buyers and startup builders to the partners that resell or embed Claude and the industry customers we're building for, and turn it into a roadmap where each new participant makes the platform more valuable to the rest
  • Own the team's outcome metrics: the share of the platform's business outside coding, new startup revenue, volume unified across the API and Claude's subscriptions, and the volume partners book on Claude, and make sure the instrumentation exists to know whether what you shipped moved them

  • Are technically fluent: you read API docs, work through a billing, identity, or attribution design with engineers, and make calls on platform primitives yourself
  • Pull your own data: SQL or equivalent, to define a metric, build a funnel, or size a market
  • Have negotiated pricing, revenue share, or program terms with Finance, Legal, or Business Development counterparts
  • Write clearly enough that an engineer, an executive, and an external partner can each see the tradeoff you're making
  • Care about Anthropic's mission, and specifically about growing this platform in a way where the people building on it share in the upside

Preferred qualifications

  • Worked on metering, usage attribution, reseller or cloud-marketplace channels, or enterprise spend management
  • Taken a developer platform into a new industry, or built product in healthcare, life sciences, financial services, or another regulated industry
  • Grown a developer product's self-serve or startup business, including its pricing and packaging
